name: Romaine Lettuce
description: A crisp, upright lettuce with elongated leaves forming loose heads. Excellent heat tolerance and distinctive crunchy texture perfect for Caesar salads.
tips: Plant in succession every 2 weeks for continuous harvest. Harvest outer leaves or cut entire head at base. Provide afternoon shade in hot weather.
succession: Plant every 2 weeks from early spring through late summer for a continuous supply of heads.
yield: 1 large head per plant, or continuous leaf harvest.
harvestInstructions: Harvest outer leaves at any time, or wait for a full head to form. To harvest the head, cut the plant at the soil level. Some varieties may regrow for a second, smaller harvest.
containerGardening: Grows well in containers at least 6-8 inches deep. Space plants according to their mature size to allow for good air circulation.

soil.type: Well-drained, fertile soil rich in organic matter.
soil.notes: Benefits from regular feeding with nitrogen-rich fertilizer. Prefers loose, well-cultivated soil.

temperature.notes: Cool-season crop. More heat tolerant than other lettuces but still bolts in extreme heat.

environmentalAlerts.message: Provide afternoon shade or harvest early to prevent bitter leaves and bolting.

storage: Store washed and thoroughly dried heads or leaves in a plastic bag in the crisper drawer for up to 10 days. Can be frozen for use in smoothies.

careTasks.name: Care for Seedlings
careTasks.description: Keep soil consistently moist for good germination. Thin seedlings when 2 inches tall.

careTasks.name: Thin seedlings
careTasks.description: Thin plants to proper spacing, using thinnings as baby greens.

careTasks.name: Side-dress with fertilizer
careTasks.description: Apply balanced fertilizer or compost around plants to encourage head formation.

careTasks.name: Begin harvest
careTasks.description: Start harvesting outer leaves or cut entire heads when firm and full-sized.

careTasks.name: Watering
careTasks.description: Water regularly to maintain consistent soil moisture. Avoid overhead watering to prevent disease.

name: Butterhead Lettuce
description: A tender lettuce forming loose, soft heads with buttery-textured leaves. Also known as Boston or Bibb lettuce, prized for its sweet, delicate flavor.
tips: Handle gently as leaves bruise easily. Excellent for containers. Harvest entire heads or individual leaves for extended harvest.
succession: Plant every 2 weeks from early spring through fall for a constant supply.
yield: 1 soft head per plant weighing 4-8 oz.
harvestInstructions: Harvest the entire loose head by cutting it at the base when it is soft but well-formed. The tender leaves bruise easily.
containerGardening: Excellent for containers and window boxes due to its compact size and shallow roots. Keep soil consistently moist.

soil.type: Rich, well-drained soil with high organic matter content.
soil.notes: Prefers cooler, moister conditions than other lettuces. Benefits from regular compost applications.

temperature.notes: Cool-season crop that bolts quickly in heat. Best grown in spring and fall in most climates.

environmentalAlerts.message: Move to shadier location or harvest immediately to prevent bolting and bitter taste.

storage: Very delicate. Store unwashed in a plastic container in the refrigerator for 3-5 days. Best eaten soon after harvest.

careTasks.name: Care for Seedlings
careTasks.description: Maintain consistent moisture and cool conditions. Seeds need light to germinate.

careTasks.name: Thin seedlings
careTasks.description: Thin to final spacing when seedlings have 2-3 true leaves.

careTasks.name: Mulch around plants
careTasks.description: Apply light mulch to keep roots cool and maintain moisture.

careTasks.name: Harvest heads
careTasks.description: Harvest whole heads when loose but full, or begin taking outer leaves earlier.

careTasks.name: Watering
careTasks.description: Water frequently with light applications to maintain consistent soil moisture.

name: Mustard Greens
description: Fast-growing leafy greens with a spicy, peppery flavor that intensifies with heat and age. Excellent cooked or raw when young and tender.
tips: Harvest young leaves for milder flavor. Cold weather sweetens the leaves. Plant in fall for best flavor and slower bolting.
succession: Plant every 2-3 weeks for continuous harvest of tender leaves.
yield: Multiple harvests of leaves per plant.
harvestInstructions: Harvest young, tender leaves for a milder, peppery flavor. Use the 'cut-and-come-again' method by harvesting outer leaves. The flavor becomes much spicier as leaves mature and in hot weather.
containerGardening: Grows quickly and easily in containers. A wide pot is good for harvesting lots of young leaves.

soil.type: Well-drained, fertile soil with good organic matter.
soil.notes: Tolerates wider range of soil conditions than most greens. Benefits from nitrogen-rich fertilizer.

temperature.notes: Cool-season crop that becomes more pungent in heat. Very cold hardy and improves with light frost.

environmentalAlerts.message: Leaves will become very spicy and bitter in hot weather. Harvest young or provide shade.

storage: Store in a perforated plastic bag in the refrigerator for up to a week. Wash just before use. Can be blanched and frozen for use in cooked dishes.

careTasks.name: Direct sowing
careTasks.description: Sow seeds directly in garden. Seeds germinate quickly in cool weather.

careTasks.name: Thin seedlings
careTasks.description: Thin overcrowded seedlings to prevent competition. Use thinnings as microgreens.

careTasks.name: First harvest
careTasks.description: Begin harvesting baby leaves when 2-3 inches long for mild flavor.

careTasks.name: Regular harvest
careTasks.description: Harvest outer leaves regularly, leaving center to continue growing.

careTasks.name: Watering
careTasks.description: Water regularly to keep leaves tender and reduce excessive pungency.
